newsitem.title: TANZANIA: U.N. Rwanda trial adjourns after absent witness.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Rwanda trial adjourns after absent witness.

text.p: The U.N. Rwanda tribunal on Friday adjourned until Monday the trial of a vice-president of the Interahamwe militia accused of genocide, after a prosecution witness failed to turn up.

The tribunal prosecutor told the court sitting in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha that the witness, the 10th to give evidence in the trial of accused Georges Rutaganda, had a family problem and could make it to court only on Monday.
On Thursday, the tribunal was told that Rutaganda, an ethnic Hutu, ordered ethnic Tutsis killed, but the defence disputed the evidence.
A witness named only as "M" to protect his identity said he saw Rutaganda distribute weapons to the militia near a well in the Rwandan capital Kigali shortly the start of the genocide in 1994.
But Rutaganda's defence counsel Tiphaine Dickson said the testimony contradicted a signed statement witness "M" made to tribunal investigators in 1995.
An estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus were slaughtered during the genocide sparked by the assassination of Hutu military strongman Juvenal Habyarimana in April 1994.

The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda was set up in 1994 to bring to trial the architects of the genocide. But many have evaded arrest and remain in safe havens in Africa, Europe and the United States.
Only 21 people have been indicted by the tribunal, plagued by administrative and financial problems. A total of 12 suspects are in detention in Arusha.
